I farm the way I always have: I start from what worked last year, then I adjust a little. On my 7.7 mu, I will keep most land in wheat-maize because that is the steady road here, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton. Around me, people who get stable harvests do not save too hard on fertilizer or water, especially with wheat. If I cut too much and the yield drops, that loss hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. I have well irrigation, so I will use it at the key times instead of waiting on the sky. I went to primary school, so I do look at the bag labels and listen to the dealer, but in the end I still do what I have seen work in our county. For wheat, I will feed it a bit heavier because wheat needs a strong stand before winter and a good push at jointing. For maize, I will not go light on nitrogen because if the stalk stays weak, the ear will be small. Cotton I will keep on a smaller area, because it takes more pesticide and more watching, but I will still plant some since I know how to manage it. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen good emergence and fuller yield, and I will keep tillage mostly rotary because it saves labor and works fine on my ground.
